extracted.intended_audience: Current and prospective peer reviewers for JGIM and similar biomedical journals (clinician-researchers, academic reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing high-quality peer reviews of manuscripts submitted to JGIM and other general medical journals, including what to evaluate, how to structure comments, and procedural responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss importance and originality of research question
rubrics_metrics.description: A good review discusses the importance of a research question and its originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the study addresses an important problem and whether the question is novel; comment on the paper's contribution and usefulness to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify strengths and weaknesses of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the strengths and weaknesses of the methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether study design, data collection, and analysis are valid and clearly described; point out methodological limitations and areas needing clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on interpretation of results and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on the interpretation of results and whether the conclusions are valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine if conclusions are supported by the data and analyses; note overreaching statements and suggest more cautious wording where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specific and constructive suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific and constructive suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give actionable recommendations for analysis, writing, formatting, or summarizing information; avoid vague criticism and, where possible, suggest how the authors can fix problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover major areas and be concise
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your review 1 to 3 pages in length, and answer the questions outlined in Table 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be comprehensive but succinct—concise reviews (1–3 pages) that specifically address core areas are preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize and organize concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize and organize your concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help authors and editors by distinguishing major issues that must be addressed from minor ones; provide brief statements, number and organize suggestions, and be clear and direct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific and give examples from the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific and give examples from the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid general statements such as “not a significant contribution” or “poorly analyzed” without details; cite line/section/table/figure examples so authors know what to change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest corrective actions where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggest corrective actions if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer concrete fixes for problems in analysis, writing, or presentation; point out fundamental flaws that are unlikely to be overcome so editors can weigh feasibility of revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be respectful in tone toward authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Be respectful of the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be fair and critical but write in the tone you would want to receive; avoid unnecessarily harsh or personal language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act as the expert (be confident and candid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Act as the expert: do not be shy; you were chosen because you have some expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide frank, expert feedback drawing on literature and experience; anonymity is believed to encourage frank feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reporting guidelines and checklists as appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Use guidelines or checklists as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply study-type specific reporting standards (e.g., CONSORT for RCTs, STARD for diagnostic studies, QUOROM/PRISMA for meta-analyses, MOOSE for observational meta-analyses, TREND for nonrandomized designs, economic evaluation guidelines) to assess reporting completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow journal instructions and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the instructions: stay within the timeline and provide scoring requested on the reviewer's report form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return reviews by the agreed deadline; complete any requested numeric or form-based ratings (e.g., appropriateness to audience, scientific rigor, clarity of writing); indicate if manuscript merits an editorial; maintain confidentiality and disclose conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain confidentiality and disclose conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain confidentiality and describe any conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share manuscript content; declare any relationships or interests that could bias your review so editors can judge appropriateness of your involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use confidential comments to editors appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Be frank when making confidential comments to the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the confidential section to state your opinion on whether the manuscript is worth publishing and other candid assessments that authors should not see; include information relevant to editorial decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sending mixed messages to author and editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not convey different messages to the author and editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistency between comments to authors and confidential comments to editors; do not be positive to authors but recommend rejection to editors—this confuses authors and creates editorial burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and format expectations for reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your review 1 to 3 pages in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be long enough to cover major issues but concise; answer the structured questions (Table 1) to ensure completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess whether paper is a useful original contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper a useful original contribution?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge novelty and usefulness to the field; discuss whether findings add meaningful new knowledge or practice implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess appropriateness for the journal's audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper appropriate for the JGIM audience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the journal's scope and readership when recommending publication or suggesting audience-level edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate literature review and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the literature review current and does it place the study in appropriate context?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether key prior work is cited and whether the manuscript situates its contribution within existing knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for ethical issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there any ethical issues that need to be addressed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify concerns about human subjects approval, informed consent, conflicts, patient privacy, data integrity, or other ethical safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate tables, figures, and use of space
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the tables and figures clear? Is there good use of space in the tables?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that tables and figures present data clearly, are appropriately labeled, and use space efficiently; suggest reformatting if unclear or redundant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess insightfulness of discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the discussion insightful?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the discussion interprets findings in context, acknowledges limitations, and provides thoughtful implications rather than mere summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess discussion of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the limitations discussed in enough detail?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that authors acknowledge study weaknesses and the impact on interpretation and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess relevance and implications of findings
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the relevance and implications of the findings?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on practical, clinical, policy, or research implications and whether these are justified by the results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess clarity and concision of writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the writing clear and concise?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note problems with readability, organization, grammar, or jargon; suggest edits that improve clarity and flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer performance is evaluated by editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Deputy Editors rate the quality of each review using a 6-point Likert scale (1=poor, 6=excellent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness, thoroughness, and clarity of reviews affect future selection and recognition (annual outstanding reviewer recognition); maintain good record by returning quality, timely reviews.
